name: Lone Star Funds

summary.text: Lone Star Funds is a private equity firm founded by John Grayken that invests in real estate, equity, credit, corporate and other financial assets; it organized its first institutional fund in 1995. In Korea it acquired 51% of Korea Exchange Bank (KEB) in 2003 and sold its stake to Hana Financial Group in 2012. The KEB investment produced criminal proceedings in Korean courts over the 2003 share price of KEB's credit-card unit, a 2007-2008 prosecution of a finance ministry official over the purchase price (he was cleared), and an ICSID arbitration (ARB/12/37) against the Republic of Korea in which a 2022 award of US$216.5 million was annulled in full in November 2025. In Japan, Lone Star took over the failed Tokyo Sowa Bank in 2001 and set up Tokyo Star Bank.

facts.claim: Lone Star Funds was founded by John Grayken, who is also the founder of Hudson, the asset-management company that services the funds; the firm's first institutional fund was organized in 1995.

facts.claim: On August 27, 2003 Lone Star acquired 51% of Korea Exchange Bank for 1.38 trillion won (about US$1.4 billion at the exchange rate at the time).
facts.quote: Lone Star acquired 51% of KEB on Aug. 27, 2003, for 1.38 trillion won (about $1.4 billion at the exchange rate at that time)

sources.title: Timeline of key events in Lone Star vs. South Korea investor-state dispute

facts.claim: In the 2003 transaction Commerzbank and the Export-Import Bank of Korea sold KEB shares to Lone Star, and a new issue of shares served as a capital injection to recapitalize KEB. Korean regulators approved the transaction as of September 2003, with the Financial Supervisory Commission and Financial Supervisory Service asking to be pre-notified before options in the deal were exercised.
facts.quote: Commerzbank and Export-Import Bank of Korea sold shares to Lone Star ... a new issue of shares served as a capital injection to recapitalize KEB ... the Korean regulatory authorities approved the transaction as of September 2003, but it was requested by the FSC and the FSS to pre-notify the regulatory authorities in advance of the execution of the options

sources.publisher: Business Perspectives (Banks and Bank Systems journal)
sources.title: Private Equity Investments in the Banking Industry: The Case of Lone Star and Korea Exchange Bank

facts.claim: In 2006 Lone Star bought a further 14.1% of KEB from Commerzbank and the state-run Export-Import Bank of Korea. In November 2011 the Financial Services Commission ordered Lone Star to cut its 51.02% stake in KEB, then the country's fifth-largest lender, to below 10% by May 18, 2012.
facts.quote: Lone Star bought a 51 percent stake in then-fragile KEB and 14.1 percent more from Germany's Commerzbank and the state-run Export-Import Bank of Korea in 2006 ... ordered Lone Star to cut its 51.02 percent stake in KEB, the country's fifth-largest lender, to below 10 percent by May 18

sources.title: Lone Star faces forced sale of majority KEB stake

facts.claim: A former finance ministry official was prosecuted on the allegation that he conspired to lower KEB's sale price to Lone Star by as much as 825 billion won below fair market value. In November 2008 a Korean court cleared him, saying it could not judge that the capital-ratio estimate for KEB had been manipulated to lower the acquisition price or to make Lone Star eligible to buy the bank.
facts.quote: "We cannot judge that the capital ratio estimate for KEB had been manipulated to lower the acquisition price or make Lone Star eligible to buy the bank," the judge said

sources.title: Lone Star Cleared of Legal Disputes

facts.claim: On February 1, 2008 the Seoul Central District Court found Paul Yoo (Yoo Hoe-won), head of Lone Star's Korea unit, Lone Star and KEB guilty in the KEB Card stock-price case; Yoo received a five-year sentence and the two companies were fined 25 billion won each.
facts.quote: Paul Yoo Hoe-won, head of the private equity firm's Korea unit, received a five-year sentence; the firm itself and Korea Exchange Bank were also found guilty. The Seoul Central District Court fined the two companies 25 billion won each

sources.title: Seoul Convicts Lone Star Exec Of Stock Manipulation

sources.publisher: Jus Mundi (ICC arbitration award, LSF-KEB Holdings v. Hana Financial Group)
sources.title: LSF-KEB v. Hana Financial Group, Final Award, 13 May 2019

facts.claim: On June 24, 2008 the Seoul High Court overturned the district court's stock-manipulation finding, removing the 25 billion won fines against Lone Star and KEB and clearing Yoo of the manipulation charge, while leaving in place a suspended two-and-a-half-year sentence against Yoo on separate charges.
facts.quote: the appeals court removed fines of 25.0 billion won ($24.2 million) each against Lone Star and KEB, but left in place a suspended sentence of two and a half years against Yoo

sources.title: Lone Star Wins A Round In Korean Court
Lone Star Cleared in Korea Stock Price Manipulation Case

facts.claim: On March 10, 2011 the Supreme Court of Korea reversed the Seoul High Court's 2008 decision that had acquitted Paul Yoo and Lone Star of stock-price manipulation in the KEB Card case, and remanded the case to the Seoul High Court.
facts.quote: the Korean Supreme Court issued its decision in the KEB Card Case on 10 March 2011, reversing the Seoul High Court's 2008 decision that had acquitted Mr Paul Yoo and Lone Star of stock price manipulation. The case was remanded to the Seoul High Court

sources.publisher: Jus Mundi (ICC arbitration award, LSF-KEB Holdings v. Hana Financial Group)
sources.title: LSF-KEB v. Hana Financial Group, Final Award, 13 May 2019

facts.claim: On retrial in October 2011 the Seoul High Court sentenced Yoo to a three-year jail term for spreading rumors about KEB's credit-card unit, KEB Credit Services, in 2003 to lower its share price and make the acquisition cheaper; Lone Star was ordered to pay 25 billion won (about US$21 million). Yoo appealed to the Supreme Court.
facts.quote: sentenced to a three-year jail term for spreading rumors about KEB's credit card unit, KEB Credit Services, in 2003 to lower its share price and make acquisition cheaper

sources.title: Lone Star Korea's former head Paul Yoo files court appeal

facts.claim: On January 27, 2012 the Financial Services Commission approved Hana Financial Group's takeover of KEB from Lone Star, ending a dispute over whether Lone Star qualified as a financial investor. Hana had agreed to acquire Lone Star's 51.02% stake for 3.9 trillion won (about US$3.4 billion), described as the biggest M&A transaction in Korean banking history.
facts.quote: The Financial Services Commission (FSC) approved Hana Financial Group's takeover of the Korea Exchange Bank (KEB) from Lone Star Funds Friday ... acquire a 51.02 percent stake in KEB for 3.9 trillion won (about $3.4 billion)

sources.title: Gov't okays Hana's KEB takeover from Lone Star

facts.claim: On February 9, 2012 Hana Financial Group completed its 4.4 trillion won (US$3.9 billion) purchase of Korea Exchange Bank from Lone Star Funds and the Export-Import Bank of Korea, closing a deal that had been pending for more than a year.
facts.quote: Hana completed its 4.4 trillion won ($3.9 billion) purchase of Korea Exchange Bank from Lone Star Funds and Export Import Bank of Korea

sources.title: Hana Finishes $3.9 Billion Korea Exchange Bank Takeover

facts.claim: In November 2012 Lone Star, through Belgian and Luxembourg affiliates (LSF-KEB Holdings SCA and others), initiated ICSID arbitration against the Republic of Korea under the Belgium-Luxembourg/Korea investment treaty (ICSID Case No. ARB/12/37). On August 30, 2022 the tribunal, in a split decision, found that Korea had breached fair and equitable treatment by unduly delaying approval of the bank sale and awarded Lone Star US$216.5 million plus interest, 4.6% of the US$4.68 billion claimed; Judge Charles Brower concurred and Professor Brigitte Stern dissented.
facts.quote: The tribunal found that South Korea had violated the fair and equitable treatment standard by unduly delaying approval of the bank sale, but it rejected the bulk of Lone Star's demand. In a split decision, it awarded Lone Star $216.5 million, only 4.6% of the $4.68 billion sought, plus interest

facts.claim: In 2023 both Lone Star and Korea applied to annul parts of the award. Lone Star filed an action to enforce the award in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on June 30, 2023 (Case 1:23-cv-01911), and on December 15, 2023 the ICSID ad hoc committee continued the stay of enforcement pending its decision on both parties' annulment applications.
facts.quote: an ICSID ad hoc committee granted Korea's request to stay enforcement of the award, over the claimants' objections, pending its determination of both parties' requests for partial annulment

facts.claim: On November 18, 2025 (Washington time) the ICSID ad hoc committee annulled in full the award's obligation to pay US$216.5 million plus interest to Lone Star, extinguishing a liability the Korean government put at about 400 billion won, on the basis that the tribunal's liability finding was tainted by a due-process violation; it left intact the parts of the award dismissing Lone Star's other claims and ordered Lone Star to pay Korea's costs of about 7.3 billion won within 30 days.
facts.quote: annulled in full the obligation to pay the 'principal of $216.5 million in compensation to Lone Star and interest thereon' recognized in the arbitral award ... ordering Lone Star to pay, within 30 days, litigation costs totaling about 7.3 billion won

facts.claim: Korean public-funds backdrop: the Financial Services Commission has reported that 168.7 trillion won of public funds was committed to the financial sector after the 1997 crisis, of which 72.5% (122.1 trillion won, about US$83.4 billion) had been recovered; banks received the largest share (44.2 trillion won) and returned 32.8 trillion won. Korea plans to repay the final 97.2 trillion won of related public-fund debt with its 2027 budget.
facts.quote: the government has been paid back 72.5 percent, or 122.1 trillion won ($83.4 billion), of the 168.7 trillion won in bailout funds

sources.title: Korea recovers over 72 percent of Asian financial crisis bailout funds
Korea to Repay Final 97 Trillion Won in 1997 Crisis Bailout Funds

facts.claim: A former Korean finance minister, writing for an IMF seminar, put the public funds disbursed by 2002 at no less than 160.4 trillion won, 30% of 2002 GDP, with about half going to insured deposits and recapitalization of troubled institutions through the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation and a quarter to KAMCO to purchase non-performing loans; a BIS paper gives 167.6 trillion won including recycled funds from November 1997 to July 2005.
facts.quote: no less than 160.4 trillion won, or 30% of the 2002 GDP ... About 50% of this went to insured deposits and recapitalization of troubled financial institutions through the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation (KDIC). The Korea Asset Management Corporation (KAMCO) received another 25% to purchase NPLs

facts.claim: In January 2001 Japan's Financial Services Agency selected Lone Star from four final candidates to acquire the assets and liabilities of Tokyo Sowa Bank, a failed regional bank. Under the contract with the bank's administrators Lone Star agreed to pay 100 billion yen for Tokyo Sowa's business rights and to spend a further 40 billion yen to set up a new bank, which took over Tokyo Sowa's operations on June 11, 2001 as Tokyo Star Bank. In 2014 CTBC Bank agreed to buy a 98.16% stake in Tokyo Star Bank from shareholders including Lone Star for about NT$15.6 billion (US$530 million).
facts.quote: Under the contract signed with the bank's administrators the same day, Lone Star will pay 100 billion yen for Tokyo Sowa's business rights. It will spend an additional 40 billion yen to set up a new bank to take over Tokyo Sowa's activities on June 11

openQuestions: The owner's draft names the Bank of Korea as a KEB seller in 2003. No source retrieved in this session confirms a Bank of Korea shareholding in KEB; the sources name Commerzbank and the Export-Import Bank of Korea, plus a new share issue. The percentage breakdown of the 2003 purchase (new shares vs. existing shares from each seller) was not retrieved.

No source retrieved shows public funds (KDIC/KAMCO) injected into KEB before 2003; one search summary said KEB continued to operate without government assistance, but the URL for that statement was not identifiable. The 168.7 trillion won figure is system-wide.

The final Supreme Court outcome of Paul Yoo's appeal from the October 2011 retrial conviction was not retrieved; the search budget ran out. The ICC award LSF-KEB v. Hana (Jus Mundi) covers the later history and could be read for it.

Lone Star's statement that its 2003 price was at a significant premium to KEB's traded share price appeared in a search summary attributed to Lone Star; the URL (Forbes 2006 'Lone Star Stands Up To South Korea' or a law-blog post) could not be pinned down, so it is not recorded as a fact.
Reported dollar conversions of the 2003 price vary (US$1.2-1.5 billion); the Korea Herald figure (1.38 trillion won, about US$1.4 billion) is used here.

The ICSID rectification decision of May 9, 2023 refers to a principal sum of USD 432,037,364 in Judge Brower's opinion; its relationship to the US$216.5 million award should be checked in the award text.
Lone Star was reported to have said it intends to resubmit an ICSID claim after the annulment; not verified.
The outcome of Paul Yoo's final Supreme Court appeal after the October 2011 Seoul High Court retrial is not recorded here; find the ruling.
